Definition: probably contracted for a compound of G3565 and G1435; nymph-given (i.e. -born); Nymphas, a Christian:--Nymphas.
BiblicalUsage: Nymphas is a Christian at Laodicea, greeted once in Colossians 4:15, where Paul sends greetings to the brethren there, and to Nymphas, and to the church in his house. The Greek text spells the name Nympha, and the house church that met under that roof is the whole of the story Scripture tells. Nymphas is one of the believers whose home became a church, and whose name is kept because the church met there.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the church in a house is still the church, and God remembers the hosts who open their doors, even when history keeps nothing else about them.
